title: Stalks of filtered colimits of sheaves of modules are filtered colimits of stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $x\in X$, $\mathcal I$ a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $D:\mathcal I\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ a diagram of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $(\mathcal F,(c_i:D(i)\to\mathcal F)_i)$ is a colimit of $D$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, then, for the ordinary Zariski module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], the compatible maps $(c_i)_x:D(i)_x\to\mathcal F_x$ exhibit $\mathcal F_x$ as the colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto D(i)_x$; equivalently, the canonical map $\varinjlim_iD(i)_x\to\mathcal F_x$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009E (section-limits-sheaves), Tag 009E, especially items (3)-(4), lines 3401-3440; used in Properties, Lemma 01PJ, lines 3148-3152

proof.text: Regard $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ as a ringed space; only this is used of the scheme structure. Let $\iota:\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the inclusion of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules into presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For every open $U\subseteq X$ choose a colimit $(\mathcal P(U),(p_{i,U})_i)$ of the $\mathcal O_X(U)$-modules $D(i)(U)$, and give $\mathcal P$ the restriction maps induced by those of the $D(i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-modules-colimits-sectionwise] (with $\mathcal C$ the category of open subsets of $X$ and $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_X$), $\mathcal P$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, the $p_i=(p_{i,U})_U:\iota D(i)\to\mathcal P$ are morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $(\mathcal P,(p_i)_i)$ is a colimit of $\iota\circ D$ in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (label lemma-limits-colimits, lines 204-239), part (2) and its proof: colimits in Mod(O_X) are the sheafification of the presheaf colimit; Sheaves, Section 009D (label section-limits-presheaves), colimits of presheaves sectionwise

proof.text: Let $\eta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#$ be the sheafification of $\mathcal P$ as a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and for each $i$ let $\eta_i:\iota D(i)\to(\iota D(i))^\#$ be that of $\iota D(i)$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. By the universal property of $\eta_i$, every morphism $g:\iota D(i)\to\mathcal Q$ of presheaves of modules has a unique $g^\#:(\iota D(i))^\#\to\mathcal Q^\#$ with $g^\#\circ\eta_i=\eta_{\mathcal Q}\circ g$; in particular $p_i^\#\circ\eta_i=\eta\circ p_i$ and $D(a)^\#\circ\eta_i=\eta_j\circ D(a)$ for $a:i\to j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] (2) sheafification $\#$ preserves colimits (it is a left adjoint), so by step 1 $(\mathcal P^\#,(p_i^\#)_i)$ is a colimit of $i\mapsto(\iota D(i))^\#$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$; and by part (3) of the same node each $\eta_i:D(i)\to(\iota D(i))^\#$ is an isomorphism. The isomorphisms $\eta_i$ form a natural isomorphism from $D$ to $i\mapsto(\iota D(i))^\#$ (by $D(a)^\#\eta_i=\eta_jD(a)$), so $(\mathcal P^\#,(p_i^\#\circ\eta_i)_i)=(\mathcal P^\#,(\eta\circ p_i)_i)$ is a colimit of $D$: a cocone $(\mu_i:D(i)\to\mathcal G)_i$ of $D$ gives the cocone $(\mu_i\circ\eta_i^{-1})_i$ of $i\mapsto(\iota D(i))^\#$, and a morphism $u:\mathcal P^\#\to\mathcal G$ satisfies $u\circ p_i^\#=\mu_i\circ\eta_i^{-1}$ for all $i$ iff $u\circ p_i^\#\circ\eta_i=\mu_i$ for all $i$. Since colimits are unique up to unique isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\theta:\mathcal P^\#\to\mathcal F$ with $c_i=\theta\circ\eta\circ p_i$ (as maps of presheaves $\iota D(i)\to\iota\mathcal F$) for all $i$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (label lemma-limits-colimits), part (2): 'Colimits are the sheafification of the corresponding colimit in the category of presheaves'; Sheaves, Section 009E (label section-limits-sheaves), items (3) and (6)

proof.text: Take stalks at $x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Since $\varphi_x(s_x)=\varphi(s)_x$, taking stalks is compatible with composition and identities, so $(c_i)_x=\theta_x\circ\eta_x\circ(p_i)_x$ for every $i$, and $\theta_x$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules with inverse $(\theta^{-1})_x$. The map $\eta_x:\mathcal P_x\to\mathcal P^\#_x$ is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear because $\eta$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\eta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#$ is the sheafification of $\mathcal P$ as a presheaf of abelian groups, so $\eta_x$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space]; hence $\eta_x$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (label lemma-limits-colimits), proof: 'Since sheafification commutes with taking stalks we see that colimits commute with taking stalks'; Sheaves, Lemma 007Z (label lemma-stalk-sheafification)

proof.text: The stalk $D(i)_x$ of the sheaf $D(i)$ is the stalk of the presheaf $\iota D(i)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-module-stalk-filtered-colimit] to the presheaf of rings $\mathcal O_X$, the filtered category $\mathcal I$, the diagram $i\mapsto\iota D(i)$ of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and its sectionwise colimit $(\mathcal P,(p_i)_i)$ of step 1: $(\mathcal P_x,((p_i)_x)_i)$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto D(i)_x$ of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009D (label section-limits-presheaves), item (5): $(\colim_i\mathcal F_i)_x=\colim_i\mathcal F_{i,x}$ for presheaves, lines 3392-3396

proof.text: By steps 2-4, $\theta_x\circ\eta_x:\mathcal P_x\to\mathcal F_x$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules carrying the colimit cocone $((p_i)_x)_i$ to $((c_i)_x)_i$. A cocone obtained from a colimit cocone by composing with an isomorphism $\psi$ is a colimit cocone: for a cocone $(\mu_i)_i$ the morphisms $v$ with $v\circ\psi\circ(p_i)_x=\mu_i$ for all $i$ correspond bijectively, by $v\mapsto v\circ\psi$, to the morphisms $u$ with $u\circ(p_i)_x=\mu_i$ for all $i$, of which there is exactly one [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Hence $(\mathcal F_x,((c_i)_x)_i)$ is a colimit of $i\mapsto D(i)_x$; equivalently, the canonical map $\varinjlim_iD(i)_x\to\mathcal F_x$ induced by the $(c_i)_x$ is an isomorphism.
